title: FULLY WORKING Fantasy Sci-Fi BROWSER MMORPG inspired by ancient mythology, alien worlds, and classic MMOs — YOU CAN PLAY IT NOW IN YOUR BROWSER!
author: Active-Zebra-6362
selftext:
# Building a Playable MMORPG with AI-Assisted Development — Saga of Dilmun

*From core systems to a functioning, server-driven MMORPG gameplay experience.*

[*www.sagaofdilmun.com*](http://www.sagaofdilmun.com)

Over the past months, I've been developing **Saga of Dilmun**, an indie fantasy sci-fi MMORPG inspired by ancient mythology, mysterious planets, and forgotten civilizations.

My goal was never to build just another visual prototype or a collection of disconnected features. I wanted to create an actual game that players can log into and play, with interconnected systems for combat, quests, character progression, inventory, equipment, crafting, and exploration.

# Beyond a prototype: A playable MMORPG

One of the biggest milestones has been getting the core gameplay loop working end to end.

Players can log in, fight enemies, complete quests, earn experience, level up, develop their characters, collect equipment, and interact with the implemented progression systems.

The individual features are connected rather than existing as isolated demonstrations. Combat feeds into progression, quests provide objectives and rewards, and inventory, equipment, and crafting contribute to the wider gameplay loop.

The current implementation includes:

* **Character progression:** Experience, leveling, and skill-tree development.
* **Three character classes:** Class-based combat and abilities.
* **Combat and enemies:** Functional encounters integrated into progression.
* **Quest system:** Objectives and rewards connected to gameplay.
* **Inventory and equipment:** Items, loot, and equipment progression.
* **Crafting and gathering:** Resource collection and crafting professions.
* **World exploration:** A fantasy sci-fi setting built around mysterious planets and ancient ruins.

The focus has been on making these systems work together as one playable experience.

# Server-side gameplay architecture

A central part of the project is its server-side gameplay architecture.

Core gameplay logic and important game-state changes are handled on the server rather than relying on the client as the authority. This provides the foundation for consistent multiplayer interactions and a shared game state.

In an MMORPG, implementing a feature is only the first step. It must also communicate correctly with other systems, update the appropriate state, and behave consistently within the running game.

That integration has been a major priority throughout development.

# Making the systems work together

Building individual mechanics is one challenge. Making them function as a coherent RPG is another.

Combat needs to connect to character progression. Quests need to provide meaningful rewards. Experience gains need to fit the level curve. Equipment and abilities need to influence player power, and crafting needs to serve a purpose within the wider game.

I've worked on integrating and balancing these interconnected systems so that progression, combat difficulty, rewards, and character development support one another.

The objective is to establish a consistent foundation that can be expanded with additional content without constantly breaking existing mechanics.

Balancing will remain an ongoing process as the game grows, but the implemented systems already form a connected, playable experience.

# AI-assisted development as a workflow

AI has played an important role in accelerating implementation and iteration across the project.

The process is not simply about generating code and moving on to the next feature. The real challenge is ensuring that new functionality fits the existing architecture and doesn't introduce inconsistencies elsewhere.

My approach focuses on implementing systems, connecting their dependencies, and refining the resulting gameplay experience.

This is particularly important for MMORPGs, where progression, combat, persistence, rewards, and multiplayer interactions are tightly connected. A change in one area can have consequences across the entire game.

For me, the real value of AI-assisted development lies in accelerating the journey from individual mechanics to an integrated game.

# What's next?

Saga of Dilmun has reached an important milestone: its core systems are connected, and players can log in and experience the implemented gameplay rather than simply watching a visual demonstration.

The next steps involve expanding the world, developing additional content, refining encounters, and continuing to test and improve the existing systems.

The long-term vision is a fantasy sci-fi MMORPG built around exploration, character progression, ancient mysteries, and cooperative gameplay.

There is still plenty of work ahead, but the foundation is there, and development continues.

**Explore Saga of Dilmun:**

Website: [https://www.sagaofdilmun.com](https://www.sagaofdilmun.com)

I'd love to hear from other developers experimenting with AI-assisted game development: how do you approach system integration when building a complex multiplayer game?

comments.body: Really like the style and art, reminds of fallout 2. The amount of features is crazy. Did you generate the assets with AI as well?

replies.author: Active-Zebra-6362
replies.body: Thanks a lot, the assets are originally from an old open-source MMORPG. I imported all the 3D assets into Blender and rendered them from an isometric perspective. As a result, everything rendered in-game is essentially a 2D sprite, making the game extremely performant both in the browser and on the server side
